steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Pour a few drops of red food coloring into a small bowl, and set aside.
With an electric mixer, beat the shortening together with the sugar in a mixing bowl until creamy. Beat in the egg and almond extract.

In another bowl, sift together the flour, baking soda, and salt. Stir the flour mixture into the sugar-shortening mixture, and mix well. Scoop up a scant tablespoon of dough with a spoon, and form into a walnut-sized ball. Place the ball onto an ungreased cookie sheet, and press the ball slightly with your thumb to create a flat spot on top (don't flatten the cookie). Dip the end of a bamboo chopstick into the red food coloring, and touch the center of each cookie to make a red dot.
Bake in the preheated oven until slightly browned, 15 to 18 minutes. Cool on a rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Almond Cookies (Dim Sum Variety)
raw_recipe.description: A beloved memory from long-gone dim sum restaurants in Hawaii, these cookies contain no almonds, but have the taste of almonds in a fat, round little cookie with a traditional red dot in the middle.
raw_recipe.name: Almond Cookies (Dim Sum Variety)

review.reviewBody: EXCELLENT! Quick, easy, and oh so good! Don't change a thing. Quite addicintg too. My daughter actually found this recipe and made it for a school project. After she made it and I tried it, I logged onto my account on AllRecipes to save to my recipe box and rate it. Since it only had 1 rating at the time of this writing, I would not have typically have made this. So glad she did, and I will definitely be making this again!

Substituted butter and added 2 more teaspoons of almond extract and they were great. Did not use red food coloring. Good texture. If you like a stronger almond flavor, I would suggest 1 tablespoon instead of 1 teaspoon. I used a medium cookie scoop and pressed tops with a fork. Made about 32 cookies. I would make it again.

These cookies are fabulous! I used butter flavored shortening (that’s what I had) and I used 3 teaspoons of almond extract because I love the flavor. I didn’t have any almonds for the top. I made a “glaze” with powdered sugar, almond extract and milk. The cookies were delicious just on their own so if this recipe is appealing to you - make them. You will not be disappointed. These are a new favorite for our family and will for sure be added to our holiday baking list.

These are so delicious, just like ones I used to get at the Chinese restaurants in NY. I didn’t have lard so I used softened salted butter in its place. I omitted salt since I used salted butter. I added an extra tsp of almond extract as others suggested (2 tsp total). I also lightly egg washed the cookies, placed sliced almonds on top and sprinkled with a tiny bit of sugar in the raw. I did not use food coloring.

Doubled the almond flavor. Used all butter. Used egg yolk and 6 good drops of yellow food coloring for the glaze before baking. Didn't use almond slice on top. Everyone wanted to know where the pink box was so they could put more on the plate ( almond cookies are normally sold in the Chinese pink box tied with string !!)

Great recipe! So easy to make. Only change I made was 1Tbsp Almond flavoring to have more almond taste. They are crispy and I had lots of compliments on these cookies. Definitely a favorite in my book.

I've never had these before but my son needed them for a cultural food day at school. They were delish! I made 2 batches, the first as written but the 2nd, I used half Crisco and half butter. The 2nd batch was even better.

Great recipe! I made it with vanilla and walnut pieces rather than almond, at the request of my sweetie. They came out wonderful, light and melty. I decorated them with sprinkles, cinnamon sugar, and the walnuts, rotating each dozen. They went over great at his family Christmas gathering. I got 4 dozen.

Wow. These came out so well! Only change I made was to add additional almond extract. Light, crisp, so wonderful They seem bakery bought! 
I did use the bamboo chopstick in red coloring to color the tops red in celebration of the New Year. Huge hit! Thank you for sharing this no fail recipe.
A good basic recipe that you can put all kinds of touches on. I also like the two TBS of almond extract for the Almond cookie.
loved this. I wanted to use up some ground unblanched almond flour so I used 1 cup almond flour and 2 1/4 cup all purpose flour. wonderful results. I also used 2 tablespoons of almond extract
They were really good!! I thought they could use more almond flavor and they did seem a bit salty. Worth making one time. Thank you for the recipe!!
Love love this recipe. My soon to be MIL loves almond cookies so I thought making them would be better than the store bought. Yes! These hot the spot. Always a hot when I make them.
easy and yummy..added an Xtra egg : )
Absolutely fabulous! Melt in your mouth texture , delicious flavour. I did add a little more almond extract .
followed recipe exactly!
Only changes I made were to double the almond extract and use 1 cup shortening + 3 TBS butter instead of the 1 cup shortening and 3 TBS shortening.
Delicious cookies!

This brings back my first Christmas in Hawaii! Neighbors made these and shared with my family..we were new to traditions in the islands and appreciated them so much! I made them exactly the same with this recipe. Thanks!
perfection!
